# What the data-dict export loses: Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS)

The YAML files here follow data-dict spec 0.1.0. They describe the common data format, so they validate against its parquet files. The records in `metadata/` remain canonical. This table counts what the export drops or flattens into text.

| | `hints5-cycle4` | `hints6` | `hints7` |
|---|---|---|---|
| variables exported | 433 | 477 | 470 |
| variables whose numeric code labels went to `details` (no labeled numeric codes) | 352 | 400 | 389 |
| missing or unresolved codes, typed only in the `__code` column's labels | 927 | 1,432 | 1,334 |
| variables listed by name only (no type the records can support) | 64 | 64 | 66 |
| availability entries (wave by form, with n), summarized as one line of text | 433 | 477 | 470 |
| field origins (publisher, data file, rule, hand, model) not exported | 1,649 | 1,814 | 1,783 |
| derived properties (scale signatures), not exported | 156 | 156 | 156 |
| release id not expressible as data-dict `version` (needs semver or a date) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
